completeness: Three partial snapshots; true original beginning and completeness remain unknown.
publication: Full supplied snapshots included with the contributor’s explicit permission. The files record what was said; their contents are not independently verified biographical or medical facts.

sources.role: Later retrieval discussion containing AI reconstructions
Overlapping continuation with further reconstructions and conceptual exploration

context_method: Track prior context, request, answer interpretation, next clarification, and separate semantic/formal repair. One exact repeated prompt supplies an observed contrast, not an isolated causal test.

overlap.treatment: Retained in both immutable sources; not a new independent exchange.

reading_coverage.method: Close reading of all 18 contiguous reading chunks, then targeted cross-source verification.
reading_coverage.qualification: Non-overlapping lines still contain quotations, reconstructed messages, repeated tables, code, and UI material; they are not all new utterances.

rules.first_source: Explicit UI user markers plus date separators; repeated user headers are not counted twice.
rules.second_source: Embedded User/AI blocks are retained as reconstructions; later unmarked speaker boundaries are not auto-certified.
rules.partial: The earliest original message and the complete conversation length remain unknown.
rules.duplicates: All three raw snapshots remain byte-for-byte unchanged. The 565-line overlap is linked. UI echoes, embedded reconstructions, repeated tables, and displayed code are distinct occurrence types, not independent evidence.
rules.counts: No full-conversation speech totals or prevalence claims. Later speaker boundaries are manually inferred locally and not fully certified. Whitespace totals include quotations and UI.
rules.analysis: Selected overlapping categories and word paths; no intent score, personal diagnosis, or automatic classification ground truth.
rules.comparison: New categories applied in new pass only; blanks in earlier panels do not imply absence.
rules.causality: Sequence links do not prove causation, hidden programming, or motive.
